title: Remarks at Statesville, North Carolina
paragraphs: My fellow citizens; My fellow Americans:

It has been a real pleasure to pass through North Carolina to-day; to see on every hand the symptoms of your awakening industrial development, and above all to meet the people of a state whose sons have always been manly, whose daughters have always been womanly. (Applause) I remember an answer reputed to have been made in the war of 1812. There was some one who said to a certain person in a certain county:"Well, in your county they all seem to be supporting the war". The man answered:"Where I come from all those who are not women are men." (Laughter and applause) I am glad to meet you here because I believe in men and I believe in women. I have very little use for those who are neither.

It is a good thing for a man, and above all, for the man who happens to be President, to travel through the country and meet his fellow Americans of every section, because thereby it is brought home to him more strongly than ever that a good American is a good American in whatever part of the United States he lives. The differences among us are trivial; the resemblances are fundamental and vital. If a man is a decent man, a square man, right, and treats his neighbors well; if he is a good husband, a good father, a good neighbor, good in the ordinary relations of life; if he does his duty as a square man, is just in his relations to the state, then he is a good citizen and we can stick with him. (Cheers and applause)
